overview.oneLineTake: Sellers keep control while rate-hike odds and inflation worries cap tech, so stay defensive on short-vol exposure into thin holiday trade.
themes: Tech rout and correction talk dominate the narrative: headlines focus on downside risk for the S&P 500, comparisons to 2018, and where equities bottom.
Rates are the pressure point: the 10-year yield sat at 4.91% (Nov 24) and coverage ties the tech selloff to Fed rate hike odds.
Growth is solid but inflation is the worry: Q3 real GDP was revised up to 4.3%, while commentary says inflation is spreading downstream.
Last close (Nov 25): QQQ 633.93 (-0.65%), SPY 716.70 (-0.29%). Dollar proxy UUP near 29.60.
Holiday session: US markets reopen for a half day, so liquidity is thin and moves can overshoot.
risks: Hawkish repricing of Fed expectations hitting long-duration tech again.
Middle East: the US renewed its travel alert, warning hostilities could escalate rapidly.
Thin holiday liquidity with leadership names (semis, hyperscalers) driving index swings.

nq.summary: NQ futures held the Thanksgiving bid and trade +0.7% above Wednesday's settle, extending the reversal off Wednesday's 24,971 NDX cash low. Low volume half day, so moves can overshoot both ways, with Nvidia and chip curb headlines still the swing factor. Thesis: mildly bullish, 4/10, buy dips above 26,000. Invalidation: NDX below 26,000. NDX levels: resistance 26,082, 26,214, 26,434; support 26,000, 25,310, 24,971.
